title: Best Enterprise Software Solutions for Custom Apps Development
summary: Compare Noloco, Retool, OutSystems, Mendix, Power Apps and Salesforce for enterprise custom apps: who builds, client access, SSO and pricing.
body_markdown:
The director of operations at a large services firm needs a portal where 60 subcontractors can see their assigned jobs, upload site photos, and submit timesheets. IT shortlists two well-known enterprise platforms. Both are capable. Both also want a discovery workshop, an implementation partner, and a quarter of developer time before anyone outside the company logs in.


That gap, between what enterprise platforms can do and how long it takes to get there, is what this guide is about. We compare six options for building custom business apps in 2026, what each one does well, and where each one fits best.


## Why Enterprises Need Custom App Development


Most growing companies run on a mix of standard software and workarounds. The ERP handles finance, the CRM handles sales, and everything in between, like job approvals, supplier onboarding, client document requests, and exception handling, lives in spreadsheets, shared inboxes, and someone’s memory.


Those in-between processes are usually what makes the business different, which is why no off-the-shelf tool fits them. They’re also where time disappears. In a[2026 Ricoh Europe study of 6,000 office workers](https://itbrief.co.uk/story/european-staff-lose-two-days-a-week-to-office-admin) , 35% said they regularly re-enter the same information across multiple systems.


A custom app gives that process one home: one place where the right people enter data once, see what’s waiting on them, and see only what they’re allowed to see.


## What to Look for in Enterprise Software for Custom App Development


Every vendor on a shortlist will say yes to “is it secure?” and “does it scale?”. These are the more specific questions that separate them.


### Scalability and Performance


Ask about the limits that matter for your apps: how many records, how many users logged in at once, and how many automated workflow runs per month. Then ask what happens to price when you cross them. A platform that handles 10 million records but charges per run can cost more than one with lower limits.


### Integration Capabilities


Check whether the platform connects directly to the systems your data already lives in, like your SQL database, Airtable, Google Sheets, CRM, or billing tool, or whether you’ll need to copy data into it. Also ask whether it has an API and an MCP server, so AI agents and other tools can read and update records safely.


### Security and Compliance


Ask for the certifications your security team needs (for example ISO 27001 or SOC 2), where data is hosted, and whether two-factor authentication can be enforced for every user. If you operate in a regulated industry, check the vendor’s compliance documents against your own requirements rather than relying on a sales deck.


### DevOps Readiness


If you have a development team, ask about separate test and live environments, version history, and how changes get approved before they go live. If you don’t, ask the opposite question: can the operations team make a change safely without a release process?


### Role-Based Access and User Management


This is where platforms differ most. Role-based access means a project manager sees different screens than a finance lead. Record-level access means a client sees only their own projects, and a subcontractor sees only the jobs assigned to them. Ask the vendor to show you the second one, across hundreds of external users, without a separate app per client. Also check SSO, SAML, and user provisioning for your own staff.


### Support and Vendor Reliability


Ask what support is included, whether you get a named customer success manager, and whether there’s an SLA. Check the vendor’s status page and how long it has been around. Then ask about leaving: can you export your data and your app logic if you switch?


## Top Enterprise Software Solutions for Custom Apps Development


Each option lists what it’s best for, what it does well, what to watch out for, and how it handles people outside your company. Enterprise plans are usually quoted individually, so pricing for each option is in the comparison table below, with a link to each official pricing page.


### Noloco


**Best for:** enterprises that need apps for their teams, clients, partners, and contractors in one place, with enterprise controls and without a long implementation project.


**What makes Noloco different:** Noloco is an AI portal builder. You describe what you need to[Nola](https://noloco.io/product/nola) , Noloco’s AI builder, for example “a supplier portal where each supplier sees only their own purchase orders, uploads delivery notes, and finance gets notified when an invoice is overdue.” Nola builds the screens,[workflows](https://noloco.io/product/workflows) , and permissions on your data. That data can live in[Noloco Tables](https://noloco.io/data/noloco-tables) , Noloco’s built-in database, or stay where it is today: Airtable, Google Sheets, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Supabase, Xano, HubSpot, and more.


**No sales cycles or complex onboarding:** your team can sign up, connect data, and build a working first version on the same day, then decide whether to bring in sales for an enterprise contract. You evaluate the product itself, not a slide deck.


**Enterprise features without enterprise complexity:** the[enterprise plan](https://noloco.io/solutions/enterprise) includes SSO and SAML, audit logs, enforceable two-factor authentication, a dedicated customer success manager and SLA, a custom MSA, and full white-label branding. Noloco’s infrastructure is ISO/IEC 27001 certified and data is hosted in the EU (see[Noloco security](https://noloco.io/security) ).[Permissions](https://noloco.io/product/permissions) can be set per role and per record, and changes are made in a visual editor, not in code.


**Flexible application types:** one workspace can run internal tools, client portals, partner and subcontractor portals, and operations dashboards on the same data. AI can also run inside the apps: as steps in workflows, as a chat assistant for users, or through the[MCP server](https://noloco.io/product/mcp) for external AI agents, all within the same permissions.


**Watch out for:** Noloco is not a full-code environment. If you need custom algorithms, heavy offline mobile use, or full control of the front-end code, a developer platform like OutSystems or Mendix is a better fit.


**People outside your company:** clients, partners, and contractors log in on every plan and see only their own records. They use client seats, not team seats, so adding a new client or subcontractor doesn’t mean paying for another team license.


### OutSystems


**Best for:** large IT teams building a portfolio of complex, business-critical apps, including customer-facing mobile apps.


**What it does well:** OutSystems is a low-code platform for professional developers, with visual development, full access to code when needed, and strong tools for testing and releasing changes. Its AI features can generate apps from a prompt, and Agent Workbench, generally available since September 2025, lets teams build and manage AI agents on company data ([OutSystems](https://www.outsystems.com/product-updates/agent-workbench-general-availability) ). It’s named a Leader in Gartner’s 2025 Magic Quadrant for enterprise low-code platforms.


**Watch out for:** it’s built for developers, so business teams usually can’t change apps themselves. Buying is sales-led, and many companies work with an implementation partner.


**People outside your company:** supported. How external users are counted depends on your contract, so ask early if you expect hundreds of clients or partners.


### Mendix


**Best for:** enterprises, especially in manufacturing and industrial sectors, that want IT and business teams building together under strong central control.


**What it does well:** Mendix, owned by Siemens, uses a model-driven approach: developers design data, logic, and screens visually, with an AI assistant to help. It has good tools for managing many apps and teams from one place, and it’s also a Leader in Gartner’s 2025 Magic Quadrant.


**Watch out for:** the learning curve is real. Most companies still need trained Mendix developers and IT involvement for anything beyond simple apps.


**People outside your company:** supported. External user pricing depends on your plan and contract.


### Microsoft Power Apps


**Best for:** companies that run on Microsoft 365, Teams, and Azure and want staff to build simple apps on that data.


**What it does well:** it fits into the Microsoft tools your staff already sign in to. Copilot can build an app from a description, and Power Automate handles workflows. For IT, governance sits inside the Microsoft admin tools they already know.


**Watch out for:** licensing has many layers. Premium connectors and Dataverse need premium licenses, and costs can grow as more people use more apps. Design options are more limited than in a developer platform.


**People outside your company:** external users usually come in as guest accounts in your Microsoft tenant, each needing the right license, or through Power Pages, which is licensed separately.


### Salesforce App Cloud


**Best for:** companies whose core data already lives in Salesforce.


**What it does well:** now sold as Salesforce Platform, it lets you build apps directly on your CRM data, with drag-and-drop tools, code when needed, and Agentforce for AI agents. Everything shares Salesforce’s security model and admin tools.


**Watch out for:** it works best when the process is close to sales and service. Building operations apps that have little to do with CRM data often means paying for Salesforce licenses for people who only need one app.


**People outside your company:** clients and partners usually log in through Experience Cloud, which has its own licenses.


### Retool


**Best for:** engineering teams building internal tools on top of their own databases and APIs.


**What it does well:** developers can build admin panels, dashboards, and back-office tools quickly with drag-and-drop components, SQL, and JavaScript. It also has tools for building workflows and AI agents, and the Enterprise plan can be self-hosted.


**Watch out for:** it assumes someone on the team writes SQL or JavaScript. SSO, SCIM, and self-hosting are on the Enterprise plan only.


**People outside your company:** external users and external apps are available on the Business and Enterprise plans, priced separately from builders and internal users. Here’s how[Noloco and Retool compare](https://noloco.io/noloco-vs-retool) .

## The Hidden Costs of Traditional Enterprise Platforms


The license fee is rarely the biggest cost. These are the ones that show up later.


### Extended Sales Cycles


Enterprise platforms are usually bought through demos, workshops, security reviews, and contract negotiation. That’s reasonable for a company-wide platform, but it means the team that asked for one supplier portal can wait a quarter before anyone starts building.


### Complex Implementation and Onboarding


Developer platforms need developers who know them. Many companies bring in an implementation partner for the first apps, then train internal staff. Budget for that time and cost, not just the license.


### Dependency on External Resources


If only a partner or two specialist developers can change an app, every small request, like a new field or a different approval step, joins a queue. Meanwhile, the operations team goes back to a spreadsheet for anything urgent.


### Vendor Lock-In and Reduced Flexibility


Apps built on a proprietary platform usually can’t be moved to another one without rebuilding. Ask how you’d export your data and logic, and whether your data can stay in a database you own.


### Delayed Time-to-Market


Each of the costs above adds weeks. For a customer-facing product, that may be acceptable. For an internal process that costs your team hours every week, every month of delay is a month of manual work you’re still paying for.


## The Rise of No-Code for Enterprises


No-code used to mean simple forms and small team trackers. With AI building and enterprise controls, it now covers a lot of the apps enterprises actually need: portals, approval flows, and operations dashboards. Gartner expects that by the end of 2028, agentic AI will be implemented through enterprise low-code platforms in four out of five businesses ([Gartner, 2025](https://www.dlt.com/sites/default/files/resource-attachments/2025-08/Gartner-MQ-for-Enterprise-Low-Code-Application-Platforms_APPIAN.pdf) ).


### Empowering Internal Teams


The people who run a process know its exceptions best. When the operations lead can add a field, change an approval step, or give a new partner access without filing a ticket, the app keeps up with how the work actually happens. IT still controls who can build, what data apps can reach, and who can log in.


### Reduced Cost of Experimentation


When a first version takes a day instead of a quarter, you can test an idea with real users before committing budget. If the pilot doesn’t work, you’ve lost a week, not a project.


### Accelerated Iteration Cycles


Most custom apps need many small changes in their first months as people start using them. On a no-code platform, those changes can go live the same day, instead of waiting for the next release.


### Democratization of Software Creation


More people building apps only works if guardrails come with it. Look for central control over who can build, which data sources are connected, and audit logs of what changed and who changed it.


## When to Choose Noloco Over Traditional Enterprise Platforms


### When You Need Control Without Complexity


Your security team needs SSO, audit logs, and per-record permissions. Your operations team needs to change the app without writing code. Noloco is built to give both: IT sets the rules, and the people closest to the work make the day-to-day changes.


### When Speed and Iteration Are Critical


If a process is costing your team hours every week, a working first version in days matters more than a perfect app in six months. With Nola, you describe the app, test it with real users, and adjust it as you learn.


### When You Want to Avoid IT Bottlenecks


IT teams in growing companies are usually stretched across infrastructure, security, and core systems. Noloco lets the operations team own their apps inside rules IT has set, so IT reviews access and data rather than building every screen.

## Real-World Examples & Use Cases


### Logistics and Supply Chain Management


A logistics company gives drivers a mobile view of today’s deliveries, dispatchers a board of every shipment and exception, and customers a portal where they can check status and download proof of delivery. Each group sees only its own shipments, and a failed delivery automatically creates a task for the dispatcher.


### Real Estate Portfolio Management


A property management firm tracks buildings, units, leases, and maintenance requests in one place. Tenants log maintenance requests with photos, contractors see only the jobs assigned to them and mark them complete, and asset managers see costs and open issues per building.


### Agency Client Management


Consultancies, agencies, and advisory firms use client portals to share project status, collect documents, and get approvals, so clients stop asking for updates by email. GAP Consulting used Noloco to automate bi-weekly billing and reported a 50% increase in billable hours ([read the GAP Consulting story](https://noloco.io/customer-stories/gap-consulting) ).


### SaaS Operations Dashboards


Software companies bring support tickets, account data, and billing status into one view for customer success and operations teams. When an account has an overdue invoice and three open tickets, the account manager sees it on one screen instead of checking three tools.


### Healthcare Administration


Clinic groups and health services providers use custom apps for the administrative side of the work: staff onboarding and credential checks, shift requests across sites, and supplier orders. If an app will hold patient data, check the vendor’s certifications, hosting location, and contract terms against your own compliance requirements first.


## Takeaways


OutSystems and Mendix are strong choices when a dedicated development team is building a large portfolio of complex apps. Power Apps and Salesforce Platform make sense when your data and users already live in those ecosystems. Retool fits engineering teams building internal tools.


If your apps need to reach your team, clients, partners, and contractors, with enterprise security and without a long implementation project, Noloco is built for that. Test external access and record-level permissions early in any evaluation, because that’s where the platforms differ most.
